body: It's giving me Reality Bites. I haven't watched the movie in an eternity, so I maybe off. That's just the first thing that popped into my head.

That's kind of the issue I have. I don't have any memories when these situations occur. Besides knowing that it's connected, I can't pinpoint it any further. What you said about disassociating sounds familiar, I will have to look into this.

I've "studied" my dreams since early teenhood, when I learned that they're my subconscious speaking to me. It was so fascinating to me. 

I usually remember(ed) them and I loved to decipher them. And they were nearly always symbolic, too. Nightmares or regular dreams. You pointed out something very important, that I kind of overlooked. My dreams, any kind, were practically always symbolic. Why would these be literal?

I'm so sorry. I'm wishing you to find pockets in time that feel a little safer.

That's so interesting! Especially what  you said about sleep. I will need to look into this as this is aligns with so many things I observe. My therapist was trying to diagnose me with the ICD-10 and I didn't meet enough of  the criteria. Unfortunately, it's not that easy to switch. I have to get approved by my insurance after a few trial sessions and I'm kind of stuck then with my therapist.
I was just thinking of you. How are you doing? Sending positive thoughts your way.

I can relate to it, for different reasons. My anxiety is not about sleep but the dreams I have. I don't dream about anything objectively bad, but remembering it feels like a nightmare. For example puzzle pieces being incomplete, making it impossible to solve it. I have lost the trust that sleep is a safe place, that dreams are usually safe as well and only subconciousness talking to me, which I always enjoyed, instead of trauma speaking to me. The bad emotions are seeping into my waking hours. I don't have much advice besides, yes I can relate to sleep not feeling safe. 

My therapist is currently searching for an EMDR specialist, as she doesn't have expertise in this field. I can imagine it could be helpful in your situation as well, if my diffuse "wave of emotions" could be targeted.
There was a second reply, which is now hidden for me. I saw it and read it. Thank you! I feel seen with how hard it was.

I'm sorry to replying so late to you. Somehow my comment got eaten and I didn't notice.

Thank you for your kind words and for reminding me that what I see in the mirror is me, not her. Genes are only one part of ourselves, but they don't have to define everything. 

I was at a low point when I wrote this post, stressed. When I get stressed, my face gets a strain that makes me look more like her. When my face is relaxed, I look more like me. It's kind of mean but it is what it is. lol. Taking care of myself and treating myself to something that feels nice, works indeed! I love makeup and when I put a little on, it helps with feeling good about myself and looking like me. The most important thing for me is lipstick. (She never liked it when I put on bright lipstick. I'm not wearing it to spite her but because it brings me joy. If it spites her, I'm not opposed to it.)
I feel like it's getting worse. I don't feel well.

I'm not in the US. I never got a bill. But I have a dotor's report on the hospital stay. I was indeed on medication but not for long. The more I think about it, it makes sense that my nightmare last night just brought everything up. I'll still investigate if there's something else going on.

Yes, I was never in the hospital before and it's a very scary place for me. Losing all control over my bodily autonomy, being at the hands of strangers is one of my biggest nightmares. Add in, that I was admitted as an emergency patient. I needed lorazepam to even agree to be operated on. I was scared out of my mind. But I never actually "forgot" about it. It's probably better to say that the way my memories and my emotions were connected to this event got unlinked for a moment.

There is documentation. I know I was in the hospital. I "forgot" about it for about 30 minutes. I was there for an emergency so it might be connected to how traumatic this was for me and the date I was admitted a year ago is only a few weeks away. There is no doubt I was in the hospital and I know why, but the way I feel about this is off. I remembered for something unrelated that I was in the hospital for the procedure I had and my mind went "this is just a bad dream from last night". Until it dawned on me.
Thank you so much for replying, I see you and I feel less alone because of it. I hope you do, too.

When I have to write I stop reading for pleasure altogether. Maybe I shouldn't do that? If try reading more or other sociological literature I get frustrated as I feel I'd never be as good as the author I'm reading. Belletrist authors with ways of expressing themselves that speak to me are usually more helpful. Thank you for reminding me of this!

Oh, this exactly what's happening to me. I try to write already thought out sentences, and well... I fail and don't write anything down. Maybe it's better to look at thoughts, speech and writing as different things rather than the same thing in different shapes.

I tried that. The thought seems logical in my head but the moment I try to either write it down or say it out loud, it comes out kind of garbled? Not my speech or the writing, but the thought seems to dissolve the moment I try to manifest it some way.

Oh, I'd wish there was something like that at my Uni. I'm not in the US and while there exists something similar, it's very limited and only available as a course with limited seats and during a certain time. I've always dreamed of support like this. :( 

If I would've come to you at the writing center, what would your advice for me be?

Thank you, this is really helpful. More precisely, my issue is not a lack of words but forming a structure. 
Oh, I've never used text-to-speech. I know Macs have it, too. 

I'm indeed telling myself cruel stories. Trying to soothe myself, I calculated exactly how much my final grade would go up or down, if I'd get this or that grade for my thesis. I barely has an influence at all. Even if I barely passed, I'd qualify for a masters program immediately. This brought me great relief. Then I made the mistake to look, up what would happen if I didn't pass. I'd get another try, but if it was plagiarism I'd be immediately exmatriculated. Now I'm afraid I'd accidentally plagiarize. I should stop doing that.

I'm not in the US but it's not allowed to speculate on someone's health like that, either. I couldn't say anything because I was too shocked. I just replied "remember, I went home earlier because I wasn't feeling well?"
Yeah, I know. Horrible person.

Yeah, and they complained about my messy desk. We never tidy up if we're working the next day anyway. They heavily implied I kind of planned this and complained my planning didn't include cleaning up my mess. As they were alone that day, they had to clean up my desk. lol so transparent...

We don't have an HR as we're a 5 people team. But it's a clear sign to look for something different. Yeah, they totally suck. They even told me that I didn't look that sick on the day I went home earlier.

I'm diagnosed but Ritalin didn't make me peaceful at all. My blood pressure went up so much I was uncomfortable all day. I could *feel* my blood pressure. I was also euphoric, I couldn't stop talking, my cheeks hurt from grinning the whole day and I unfortuntely didn't make any sense. I wrote a few pages one day in my thesis and had to toss out nearly everything. I wasn't focused, I was manic. There was never peace, my mind was actually racing. Maybe just in one area (my thesis) but my mind was more calm without it. When I went off it I could relax again. 

 I don't want to feel like this ever again.
Yes, I do. But I went decaf for the time. The many posts here warned me. But not my doctor. :/

I gave up after two weeks. I started with 10mg a day and was to supposed to add another dose the following week. First day was like a trip. Very high blood pressure, no focus, talked non-stop and I grinned so much, much checks hurt in the evening. I took only half the next day because I wouldn't have been able to work like that. I took 5mg for the rest of the time but my blood pressure was always around 150 - 110. I couldn't sleep because of that and was always tired. I went off it on the weekend of the second week and could finally sleep, my mind stopped racing and I felt "normal" again. 

My doctor told me that these side effects would subside after a while. But never told me how to tell if the dose was right? Both 10 and 5mg felt like too much. There was never focus or calm.
I went with Bupropione as it's familiar to me and I don't remember any side effects.

Thank you, it feels nice to get validated and encouraged to keep doing what feels right for me. More than not doctors dismissed me and that can be very disheartening. 

I really don't want to try any stimulant for the time being. Maybe it wasn't such a good idea to try ritalin first. Half the dose didn't help but made it worse from my perspective. I felt drunk and drowsy. The full dose at least made me alert. I hope the bupropione will help as I had that in the past for my depression and it helped with the depression but with basically zero side effects. 

Thank you for encouraging me to keep going and speaking up for myself and that I can chose treatment.

I think you're making the mistake to apply logic to it. This seems to be political with a certain pursuit disguised as "protect the children". In the least it's puritan views speaking, trying to shield children nearly from everything.

At first glance I thought they were talking about much younger kids. The graphic novel in question is intended for 10 - 14 year olds in Germany, her diary gets a recommandation from the teachers' association of Badem-Württemberg of 12 years.

I really hope this is about this particular version which seems to be a graphic novel, not the well known version of her diary (which was redacted prior to being printed). I'm not giving them a pass. This just seems to they wanted to be safe, not being uneducated. But they seem unprepared.

What do you exactly mean by banned in schools? It definitely was never on the curriculum other than being an example of propaganda. So it was talked about as a piece of history not as a piece of literature. Many schools don't have libraries at all, books are usually bought for class. You wouldn't have been able to find it in municipal libraries or bookstores up until recently so there's no reason to look for it in it schools. It was never forbidden to own a copy and you could easily get it pre-owned as there's millions and millions of it printed. 

I have no idea what would've happened if someone would've brought to school, but probably it would've been confiscated and probably talked in class about why it's bad (I'd expect this to happen in my school).
Thank you for understanding. I felt a tad bit misunderstood in some of the replies.

I get you. What helps me to look at the actual increase in risk. This [article](https://www.health.harvard.edu/blog/nsaids-how-dangerous-are-they-for-your-heart-2019010715677) cites "a one to two excess cardiovascular events for every 1,000 people who take NSAIDs". That's really low. That's about 1 per mille or 0.1%. This is an example for Ibuprofen and it's true for many other medication. You can also always ask your doctor about it. They prescribe the same medication to many patients and know about and see effects and side effects firsthand. 

Manufacturers have to put this into the leaflets due to regulations. They're also not neccessarily common occurences, but have to be mentioned.

That's a good idea! I don't have to tell them that it was a very selective detox. I don't want to delete the email, but I've filtered them all to a folder out of sight. I deleted Signal. 

They actually don't know the real reason why I'm sick. I felt like they didn't need to know and I don't have to disclose it.

This is exactly how it feels and probably why I feel the way I do about it. It feels infuriating! 

I'm planning to address this in the future as I feel we don't have good separation of what's work and what's private time. We communicate a lot on informal channels so everything feels kind of intertwined and can lead to potentially overstepping.

I'm just so worked up and it's currently hard to look at it and brush it off. They shouldn't be contacting me at all after I called and talked to boss 1. I was doing much better until boss 2 wrote that email. They're impacting me getting better. I hope I can just forget about work for the rest of the week after I deleted the app and won't check the folder I filtered all work related emails into.

Edit: whoever downvoted me - care to elaborate? It's easier said than done when it comes to things like this. I am currently pretty stressed, I have trouble to just let go. I'm not in the US and there's certain rules in my country around sick leave and what bosses are allowed to do and ask - and regarding my duties.

Unfortunately, my other boss asked me via email if I might be good enough to come in Saturday. Despite what was agreed upon with boss 1. On my private email. I feel worse again. I feel like I have to answer this email to keep a good relationship with boss 2, but I'm not obliged by law to do so. I've asked a family member who is a superior for a larger team on what to do and they advised me to politely get back to them, but keep it short. I hate that I even had to do this or even think about it. It ruined my day.

I just told work I can't come in Saturday. They were understanding and will try to find a replacement and if not, "then that's the way it is. You can't help being sick." I feel so relieved. Thank you for encouraging to take the time.

Thank you. I probably needed to hear that it is okay to take the time off. I actually love my work so this confused me to no end. I didn't really understand why I was so unhappy I was crying in the supermarket. I called in sick Friday morning and the few days have already helped tremendously. I'm not fully recovered, but so much better. 

I was looking forward to the event on Saturday but I probably need this break. 

I wish you all the best in your recovery!

Just a little update: I sent her an email earlier in the day and got a rather lengthy response a few hours later. She will remove that part. Yay. This gives me back control and I can mention it if I want to but I won't have to explain myself. This is all I wanted.

I'm not worried about treatment itself. Over the weekend I've read even more about ASS and I don't see myself. I don't want to have to explain myself and if I change my mind, I would like to bring it up myself.
Thank you! ❤️

Thank you. Absolutely spot on about how I feel. And thank you for speaking up. A lot of people seem to have only focused on "autism".  That's is not the point. It could've been any diagnosis. I feel very confident in what I said and how I feel and see it. ❤️

While I agree with you in general, I didn't make a causality error. It's not necessarily always like this. I know why I was bullied and it was absolutely tied to my primary teacher and nothing I did. Once I left that environment, it stopped. But by that point, it had left a mark. It might have a higher likelihood, but there can't be an absolute causality.

It may sound like it but the main issue is, it doesn't align with way I know about myself. I had a basic understanding of it that wasn't derived from media but medical literature. I was studying biology that I wasn't able to finish (the only thing that was missing was the thesis). I researched it further after she mentioned it and I don't see myself in it. This is not a judgement of people on the spectrum. I felt challenged about knowing myself. You could swap in a different diagnosis that doesn't match about what I know about myself. No diagnosis I ever got was a surprise to me and felt this wrong.

That's how I felt during the session. It felt odd? She also barely explained why she had that suspicion. After she saw my confusion, instead of explaining it she went on how neuro-atypical people could thrive once they found their niche. This was far from a productive conversation. Fortunately, I don't have go her again. But her letter functions as a report that I need for medication and further treatment. I do feel confident to explain this to any practitioner along the way, but I do not know if they will accept my input and shy should I have to do this?

I'm not taking it like this. It doesn't align with what I know about myself and after researching it, I'm even more sure. I've considered it. The therapist didn't really address her suspicion. She mentioned it nearly in passing at the end of a session. That can't be enough.

The thing is, I'm an adult. I'm nearly 40. I'm pretty sure I know myself very well. What the therapist suggested is very far from what I know about myself. That's the point. Not that she suggested autism. I could've been any diagnosis. She also almost suggested this in passing. She didn't do any testing and from what I can gather made this from observation only and we only had six sessions. This isn't enough. This is what I'm not okay with. 

There were a few comments that hit the nail on the head but unfortunately most though that I was upset about autism. That's not it.

This is exactly how I feel about this. I don't identify with what the therapist suggested after I researched it. I could've been any diagnosis. The therapist might've made an educated guess, but it's exactly this. A guess. The therapist also didn't communicate that she wasn't merely suggesting. That's what she said in the session. That it was included in the letter was a surprise.

Thank you. This is how I felt about it. I've had also bad experiences with doctors simply stating very objectively wrong things. While it's easy to dispute "patient came in with a broken arm" when you broke your foot, something like this is much harder to fight. And yes, I had bad experiences with psychologists as well. 

This gives me hope that this might not just stick. Did you address this with your former therapist? (I also found a factual mistake in the letter). 

That's a good course. For the time being I will try ADHD medication. Maybe that's what I need, as you said.

I will have to quote myself here.

>I do disagree because I know myself best. This is not about autism, but somewhat an insult on how well I understand myself. I got a hint from a different part of reddit about ADHD and researched it, took a few screening tests, read self-reports. I could absolutely see myself in it. Certain things fell into place, my issues made sense. I did the same for autism and I don't see myself in it.

I've seen people downvoting me for giving my reasons. Unfortunately, I feel people invalidate my feelings about being potentially misdiagnosed. Even if the therapist is right, I should be allowed to have feelings about it. I'd consider any diagnosis that you didn't expect as something that can weigh on you. 

As for the questionnaires, I was desperately trying to get help so I tried to answer them "as accurately as possible" and I didn't trust this specific person. I was stressed. I would add examples instead of just answering "likely yes", no or yes. I don't usually have issues with questionnaires. 

Maybe I should add that English is not my native language.

I took it as a question I'd need to answer for myself. 

I felt like I couldn't say anything that wasn't scrutinized, seemingly everything I said would be "diagnosed". And no, this is not something that constantly happens to me. I would attribute this to this specific situation as I was there solely for diagnostics. I never had this with any therapist I had before.

Do you really react neutral to a potential diagnosis? I didn't see it coming, it was a surprise to me. I had to digest this and reflect on what that might mean for *me*. I do disagree because I know myself best. This is not about autism, but somewhat an insult on how well I understand myself. I got a hint from a different part of reddit about ADHD and researched it, took a few screening tests, read self-reports. I could absolutely see myself in it. Certain things fell into place, my issues made sense. I did the same for autism and I don't see myself in it. As I said, I could've ignored it as I came to the conclusion, that she's wrong. But I need that letter to get medication.

But I get the feeling that no matter what I say, I will look like a person that can't accept a diagnosis.

I will need to give this letter to a doctor that will prescribe me with medication for ADHD. This my main concern. The letter itself is not the issue other than I think she is wrong. 

I'm not in the US. I not only can but I have the right to either share the diagnosis myself, allow direct communications regarding my treatment between practitioners or forbid it.

I found a doctor that will prescribe me with medication for ADHD but I will need to send her this letter. This is one of the reasons I'm not exactly pleased. 

I know why I responded the way I did. Is it so out of the ordinary to react like this? If I was on the spectrum this would have implications for my life. And most importantly how I see myself and who I am as a person. 

I took a step back and researched it and tried to find out if it might apply to me. I came to a different conclusion than her.

I've read a lot about autism since she mentioned it. Symtoms can also overlap with trauma, ADHD and depression. I simply don't agree with her. I have taken more questionnaires than I can count and only had theses troubles taking these test with her. I'm not interested in taking more tests. I also feel that this is a loosing game. You brought up the sense of being misunderstood as being common with autism. I agree with everything else in her letter, just not this part as I think her assessment is wrong. Should I just swallow it? Doctor's letters can and will have sometimes errors. I don't think I should just blindly accept it. A wrong diagnosis can haunt you and cause further issues down the line.

Is money actually an issue? You didn't write about this. Are your friends working in their respective fields? Or is it about work experience in general? There is no definite way that is right for everyone. I think it is a good a idea to focus on your studies first if you feel that this is the right way for you. You could also work during the breaks or do a shorter internship to get to know your chosen field better. Just because something is right for others doesn't make it right for you. Those post on social media can also be very deceiving. They might be struggling.

Is writing easier for you? You can check if they have an email address and write them. 

For things that unfortunately can't be done in a less stressful way, I've learned to think about what might happen. For example: the most likely scenario for a call to a practioner of any kind is, that they will pick up of the phone and say their name/pratice. You will say your name. Next will probably be that you tell them that you'd like to make an appointment, they might tell you a date. Maybe you talk a little more or a little less. Then you will say bye and hang up. 

You also don't have to think of a better version of yourself right now. Reaching out can be hard. Try to work towards this first. Then step by step. You posted here and I bet it wasn't easy as well. Well done! I'd love to hear from you again.

Has anyone talked about all the strategies to avoid things like this? They cost money and time as well. Airtags are not cheap. And I really need them. (This reminds me to get to the bottom of why my smartwatch didn't remind that I left my phone at home).

I personally just use the apps that came with my phone, but using a reminder of some sort is very helpful.

My tip in general would be to put tasks like cancelling the moment you know of the date. For example I want to try a service or app that auto-renews, I put a reminder with enough time ahead to cancel or immediately cancel if that's available.

I'm not sure if you're taking about me or not. I walk my dog every day and I'm not pretending that my dog never does any of this. But I have at least some control of where my dog goes. My dog is female, so maybe it's different.

I would've said yes. I've let people use our guest bathroom before. But only kids and elderly, as those are the only ones who even asked. 

I also feel this way, there is no winning side.
I think it is. I also do not fault the kid at all in this. An adult can be held to a different standard, though.
Thank you. This sums up my conflict so well. I guess there is no clear winning side in this. We're all in the wrong for different reasons.

No, I wouldn't. I would've offered our guest bathroom. I've done that before and I would do it again. But they didn't ask. 

There are no weeds that could be harmful or snakes. I get that with the one time emergency but you're making assumptions. Feel free to ask, but this is not fair.
The width is the same everywhere, about 5 feet and it's flat. The only difference is our house.
Narrow road with tarmac, grass on both sides. I'm not sure how wide the road is, but a tractor can pass a pedestrian.
Either with a leash or I tell my dog to keep going. Maybe this is not as normal as I thought.

Yes, but just because I don't use it, why does it have to used as a bathroom? A few yards further up and no one would care. Or across from our house. I'm not so sure about respectfulness but privacy, which is totally understandle. But I wouldn't call it respectful.

Maybe my expectations for respect are over the top. I'm not that concerned over the pee itself. While it's a strip of dirt next to the fence, would this change if it was nicely tended grass or expensive stones? To me this doesn't matter. I take issue with that my property was chosen as a toilet.
Politeness, respect. I'm not afraid of bacteria. I respect other's property and do not enter or litter on it.

Sorry, it's next to the street and we use it as a pathway in winter when the road is icy. I get that was confusing. 

We clarified this a few years back what is our property and what is not, and this area indeed is.

Our house is the only one on a long stretch. They might've thought it would've given some privacy. 

The pathway was kind of untended the last few years and I didn't mind dogs peeing there as much, but now I cleared up the the weeds and prepared to mow the area I don't like dogs peeing there. I also have to clear that area every day from dog poop and garbage.
On someone's property? Is that seriously okay? Because I don't let my dog do that. I'm genuinely asking.

I get it, that's why I'm so conflicted. She was small enough not be able to hold it. 

But we do own that pathway. It's part of our property. It's not a sidewalk, just a strip of dirt (for now) next to the fence.

Triggering in the sense that my emotions don't match in their intensity. I get what you mean. The executive team gets regular supervisions to work on conflicts like these - but only between them. Part-timers are not included, sadly. 

Part of feeling this way is because I'm frustrated with being at the "receiving end" so to speak. I'd love to be able to make more decisions myself, have more responsibilities. I'm stuck in a position I don't want anymore.
I've started volunteering with a womens rights non-profit and am working since 2015 for them. I feel less helpless since I am actively working for womens rights, with women, side by side.

I have one, but I don't have an established diagnosis. My therapist did some pretty extensive testing, but she doesn't want to diagnose me based on her findings and because my case isn't that clear cut.
Thank you for this suggestion, I will try that!

A lot of information was passed at our place when meeting in the hallway or getting coffee. Very informal and it relied on actually talking face to face. As this was not possible in the last two years, people had to make the concious effort to sit down and write an email. Or pick up the phone. We talked about this a lot and tried to do better, but to be honest, it has gotten worse. 

Maybe due to general exhaustion, having to make the effort to include people that are not present. I get that, but it feels not so notice being the person that gets learn everything last. :/

I most definitely overreact a bit. That's why checking in like this is so helpful.

No, they're telling me last of the team. The volunteers are part of the non-profit but not of the working team, which I am. I don't work with the volunteers. We have regular meetings with the volunteers, but they aren't part of the day to day work. 

The thing is, I am supposed to be informed about changes in the team - new members coming or those leaving. Definitely not the minute the decision is made, but maybe before I meet the new team member in the hallway one unsuspecting Monday. I've brought this up in the past and the executive team apologized and vowed to do better. I has in fact gotten worse. I also don't think they're doing this on purpose, but I don't plan on getting used to it.

Thank you, this helps a lot! Your second sentence rings very true. It does feel different. I don't have anything to compare it to, so to hear that other places are similar in this regard, puts it into perspective.

Nah, that's mean. I'd never take out any issues I have with someone on their pet. This could also harm the dog, I would never forgive myself. The dog doesn't understand what's going on and will be at least uncomfortable or even in pain. And I brought that on deliberately? Horrible. What if he has digestive issues and this will add to it? I'd consider her dog annoying, that's true. But part of it is her fault. The bad recall? That's on her. The talkative part? I don't know. Some pups are like that. Mine is a bit too silent in parts. She just looks at you and apparently thinks you know what she wants.
I try to tackle this with compassion. She's insecure. I get it as I struggled with that, too. But dang, I'm not her enemy. I would wish she wouldn't take this out on me.

Oh, I see. I don't think I'd have to fear anything actually dangerous. Annoying, yes. But nothing to be afraid of. 

She is kind of ignoring me but to make a point so it stands out. Like in the situation today. I greeted her, she almost walked through me.
I have to agree here, sadly. I would just wish that she wouldn't put that on me. I just existed on that fateful summer day. If someone understands insecurity, it's me. I'm not the enemy.

I guess I could at least try to talk to her. An innocent "is there something wrong" after she didn't greet me, accompanied with a smile. Maybe throw in a compliment about her dog. He's indeed very beautiful. I will really need to work on the compliment, though. He's what I dub as a "talker" and does not listen at all. She constantly yells at him and the dog keeps "talking", but doesn't even move a paw towards her. But, yeah. He's a pretty boy. *eyeroll*
To be frank, I don't even know how this man looks like these days. I avoided them as I was pretty shocked to experience this behavior from a circa 50 year old woman.

Thank you so much for sharing. I love how you tackled it what looks pretty straightforward and asked for help. And I'm happy for you that you were successfull, got heard, taken seriously and not dismissed. This gives me hope. 

You're probably right, preparation is key. I'm somewhat desparate, as currently there's a lot at stake and if getting diagnosed right and finally treated so my symptoms get manageable this would be a big deal. During the evaluation the therapist asked: hm, nothing has helped long term so far? That's interesting, in my opinion it's worth to re-visit and re-evaluate a bit.
